findings.claim: The page stamp is read once, before the loop (classify.go:173). Each port answer is then saved under that stamp (classify.go:195), with no second read to check that the page did not change in between. Failure mode: Stamp returns S, the page is then edited (a classifier writes or removes a row, or a rollback), and Classified reads the new bytes. The answer for the new content is then saved under S. The next stop sees stamp S2 and asks the port again, which is fine. But if the page later returns to the bytes of S (L69 relies on rollback restoring the old stamp and making its memory right again), the session reads the saved answer, which was about other content. It then skips or asks for the result wrongly for as long as the page stays in state S. One fix is to read Stamp again after Classified and skip the memo Add when the two stamps differ. No test pins this ordering.

The doc of incomplete (classify.go:104-106) and test M3 promise one line on stderr. That holds only if each problem is one line itself. A refusal can now be a git error from heldResult (M1 case 'git cannot give the diff'). gitexec.output wraps git's trimmed stderr with said(), which keeps the newlines inside it (gitexec.go:1161, 1183-1188). review_stop_hook.go:62 prints err with %v and does not flatten it. So git stderr with more than one line breaks the one-line contract that this type was added to keep. M3 uses only single-line causes, so nothing pins this case.

Hunt class (1), empty value: an empty stamp returned with no error is accepted as a valid page state. If an adapter returns "", nil (T4w's Stamp, still unwritten), every page state gets the same memo key. A result's first answer is then reused for the whole session, which brings back the stale-after-row-removal defect of -6 F1 without any signal. classifyRuling could refuse an empty stamp as a pass error, like a Stamp error (M7), and a test could pin that.
